en: Air is a mixture of gases like nitrogen and oxygen that has measurable mass and takes up physical space.
Melting ice into liquid water is a physical change because the chemical structure of the H2O molecules remains completely unchanged.
Dissolving sugar in water does not destroy the sugar, as the sugar molecules remain intact and can be recovered through evaporation.
Not all metals are magnetic, because only specific metals like iron, nickel, and cobalt are attracted to magnets.
Boiling water into steam is a physical change because the H2O molecules remain chemically identical and do not form a new substance.
An object's ability to sink or float depends on its density relative to water, not simply on how heavy the object is.
Gases have definite mass and take up space, expanding to completely fill the volume of any closed container holding them.
Rusting is a chemical change where solid iron reacts with oxygen and water to form a new substance called iron oxide.
Cold is not a physical substance that flows, but rather thermal energy always moves from warmer objects into cooler objects.
Evaporation is a physical change that occurs at any temperature when surface liquid molecules gain enough energy to become a gas.
Mixtures like sand and saltwater can be separated using physical methods like filtration and evaporation without causing chemical reactions.
Burning wood is a chemical change that produces entirely new substances like ash and carbon dioxide gas, rather than just melting the wood.
